cues.zh: 我想给你们看样东西。
cues.en: I want to show you something.

cues.zh: 就是这台收音机。
cues.en: It’s this radio.

cues.zh: 它看起来挺酷的吧？我经常用它。
cues.en: It’s pretty cool looking, right? I use it pretty often.

cues.zh: 现在，给你们出个小挑战：
cues.en: Now, here’s a fun little challenge for you:

cues.zh: 告诉我它的型号、生产年份、里面用了哪些真空管，
cues.en: Tell me the model number, what year this radio was made, what vacuum tubes are inside of it,

cues.zh: 再帮我找到它的电路图，这样我就能订购新的电容了。
cues.en: and find its schematic diagram for me so I can order new capacitors for it.

cues.zh: 来吧。
cues.en: Go on.

cues.zh: 如果这看起来很难——其实一点也不难。
cues.en: If that seems like a difficult task - it’s very much not.

cues.zh: 只要你能看到这张图，你现在屏幕上就有获取所有这些信息乃至更多内容所需的一切，不到一分钟就能搞定。
cues.en: So long as you can see this image, you have everything you need on your screen right now to get all that information and much more in less than a minute.

cues.zh: 前提是你知道去哪儿找、怎么找。
cues.en: That is, if you know where and how to look.

cues.zh: 我马上就会告诉你去哪儿找、怎么找，
cues.en: Now, I’m gonna show you where and how to look in just a moment

cues.zh: 但首先我得说明，这无疑会是我发布过的最暴躁、最“老头对着云大喊”的一期视频，我不回避这一点。
cues.en: but first I should note that this is no doubt going to be the most crotchety, old-man-yells-at-cloud video I’ve ever released and I won’t hide from that.

cues.zh: 有一点我也不避讳：这很大程度上是一期观点类视频。
cues.en: Another thing I won’t hide from is the fact that this is largely an opinion piece.

cues.zh: 如果这不合你的胃口，欢迎随意看看本站的其他视频。
cues.en: If that doesn’t sound like your jam, please feel free to watch any of the other videos on this here website.

cues.zh: 但如果你愿意听我讲——这其实正是本期视频的重要内容。
cues.en: But if you’ll indulge me - that’s actually a large part of what this video is about.

cues.zh: 它讲的是现代互联网，以及我认为它如何让很多人不再主动去寻找东西。
cues.en: It’s about the modern internet and how I think it’s caused a lot of folks to stop looking for things.

cues.zh: 我稍后会解释我的意思，但先让我们弄清楚那台收音机是什么。
cues.en: I’ll explain what I mean later but first let’s figure out what that radio is.

cues.zh: 我们手头只有一张图片。
cues.en: So - all we’ve got is a picture.

cues.zh: 但我保证，你不需要任何花哨的图像识别工具就能找到这台收音机。
cues.en: But I promise you don’t need any fancy image recognition tools to find this radio.

cues.zh: 你只需要注意到它的几个细节。
cues.en: All it takes is noticing a few of its details.

cues.zh: 这台收音机品牌是“Silvertone”，调谐旋钮上有两组数字，一组标着“标准广播”，另一组标着“ff某调制”。
cues.en: The radio is branded “Silvertone” and the tuning dial has two sets of numbers, one labeled “standard broadcast” and the other labeled “ffsomething modulation.”

cues.zh: 第一个词被旋钮指针挡住了一部分，但很可能是 frequency（频率）。
cues.en: The first word is partially obscured by the dial’s pointer but it’s likely frequency.

cues.zh: 你可能知道FM是频率调制的缩写，这显然是一台老式收音机。
cues.en: You probably know that frequency modulation is what FM is short for, and this is clearly an old radio.

cues.zh: 所以这是Silvertone生产的某种老式FM收音机。
cues.en: So it’s some kind of old FM radio made by Silvertone.

cues.zh: 我们怎么确定是哪一款呢？
cues.en: How can we identify which one?

cues.zh: 咱们试试看能不能通过Google图片搜索找出来。
cues.en: Well, let’s see if we can pick it out from a Google Image search.

cues.zh: 很多人会称这台为复古收音机，所以我们搜一下“vintage silvertone FM radio”。
cues.en: A lot of people would call this a vintage radio so we’ll look for “vintage silvertone FM radio”

cues.zh: 这里有很多酷炫的老式收音机图片，但你看那个——正是同一台。
cues.en: There are lots of pictures of cool old radios here but look at that - it’s the very same one.

cues.zh: 点开它就能看到图片描述，上面写着这是Silvertone Model 18。
cues.en: And with a click on it we’ll see the image description which tells us this is a Silvertone Model 18.

cues.zh: 太好了！既然知道了型号，我们就能获取更多细节。
cues.en: Wonderful! Now that we have its model number, we can get more details.

cues.zh: 我想要这台收音机的电路图，所以咱们在网上搜一下“silvertone model 18 schematic”。
cues.en: I wanted the radio’s schematic diagram, so let’s do a web search for "silvertone model 18 schematic."

cues.zh: 第一个链接指向一个叫 radiomuseum.org 的网站——看起来挺有戏！
cues.en: The first link is to a website called radiomuseum.org - that looks pretty promising!

cues.zh: 点进去，还有一张同款收音机的照片，所以我们可以确认这确实是 Silvertone Model 18。
cues.en: Click through and there’s another picture of the same radio, so we have confirmation that this is indeed a Silvertone Model 18.

cues.zh: 就在这个页面上，我们看到它的生产年份是 1950 到 1954 年，
cues.en: And right on this page we find it was produced between 1950 and 1954,

cues.zh: 另外还有它 8 个真空管的列表。
cues.en: plus we have a list of its 8 vacuum tubes.

cues.zh: 当然还有可以下载的电路图，
cues.en: And of course there is the schematic available for download,

cues.zh: 不过在其他网站上也能找到。
cues.en: though it can also be found on other websites.

cues.zh: 把这些信息保留在网上是件很费功夫的事，我要为那些致力于维护这类活跃数据库的人点赞
cues.en: Keeping this information available online is a serious undertaking and I applaud the people who dedicate themselves to maintaining active databases like this

cues.zh: （也为那些做备份工作的人点赞。尤其是现在）。
cues.en: (as well as those doing the work to back it all up. Especially right now).

cues.zh: 这个小练习的意义在于……
cues.en: The point of that little exercise was…

cues.zh: 嗯，就是练习！
cues.en: well, exercise!

cues.zh: 我们刚才做的，堪称人类超能力。
cues.en: What we just did is nothing short of a human superpower.

cues.zh: 仅凭一张老式收音机的照片，你就能用简单的搜索工具和自己的观察，获取大量信息。
cues.en: From just an image of an old radio you can find out a lot of information using simple search tools and your own observations.

cues.zh: 只要有一点好奇心，你就能继续深挖下去。
cues.en: And if you’re just a little curious, you can keep going.

cues.zh: 你注意到制造商是Sears, Roebuck & Co.了吗？
cues.en: Did you notice that the manufacturer was Sears, Roebuck & Co.?

cues.zh: 没错，就是那个Sears。
cues.en: Yeah, that Sears.

cues.zh: 就是那个建了我只要天气允许就天天能看到的塔的公司。
cues.en: The one that built the tower I see everyday, weather permitting.

cues.zh: 当年他们自己生产很多东西，Silvertone是他们的电子产品品牌，也做乐器。
cues.en: They made a lot of stuff in-house back in the day, and Silvertone was their brand of electronics and also musical instruments.

cues.zh: 这台棕色世纪中叶风格的美物就是他们的收音机之一。
cues.en: This brown mid-century beauty was one of their radio receivers.

cues.zh: 如果你对古董收音机、真空管一无所知，也不明白为什么这些老家伙通常需要换新电容，这些你也都能查得到！
cues.en: And if you don’t know anything about antique radios and vacuum tubes and why these old things usually need new capacitors, you can also find all that out!

cues.zh: 搜索“更换古董收音机电容”，你就会来到这个可爱的网站，
cues.en: A search for “replacing capacitors antique radios” brings you to this lovely website,

cues.zh: 它比 Google 现在用 AI 拼凑出来的那些乱七八糟的东西有用得多，
cues.en: a much more useful resource than whatever AI nonsense Google is synthesizing

cues.zh: 因为不知为何，现在的搜索引擎好像就该是这个样子。
cues.en: because that’s apparently what search engines are supposed to be now for some reason.

cues.zh: 哎，老头子又开始对着云喊话了。
cues.en: Ope, there’s the old man yelling at clouds.

cues.zh: 早说了吧。
cues.en: Told ya.

cues.zh: 我相信很多人一看那张图就知道里面的信息多有用，也知道怎么用它去找那台收音机，
cues.en: I am sure a lot of you knew how useful the information in that image was and how you could use it to find the radio,

cues.zh: 而对那些已经会的人来说，这个视频到目前为止大概显得平平无奇。
cues.en: and to those of you who did this video probably seems incredibly unremarkable so far.

cues.zh: 但我现在越来越确信，这是一项随着时间推移人们正在忘记自己拥有的技能，因此即使它能帮上忙，人们也不会想到去用。
cues.en: But I believe quite strongly now that this is a skill which as time marches on people are forgetting they have and thus don’t think to use even when it could help them.

cues.zh: 我想重申一下我刚才用的说法：
cues.en: I want to reiterate the language I just used there:

cues.zh: 我不是说人们不会做这件事——谁都能做，但愿大家在学校里学过怎么做。
cues.en: I am not saying people don’t know how to do this - anyone can do this, and hopefully you learned how in school.

cues.zh: 这算是相当基础的研究。
cues.en: It’s pretty basic research.

cues.zh: 我想说的是，似乎越来越多人在这个世界上行事时，并没有意识到这些事他们自己也能做。
cues.en: What I am saying is that it appears as though an increasing number of people seem to operate in the world without realizing these are things they can do themselves.

cues.zh: 这真的让我很担心。
cues.en: And that really concerns me.

cues.zh: 我在论坛上混得够久了，知道有个叫“让我帮你谷歌一下”的东西——
cues.en: Now I’ve spent enough time on forums to know about “let me google that for you” -

cues.zh: 那是对那些问一句网搜就能解答的简单问题的人，一种带刺的回应。
cues.en: a snarky response to people who ask easy-to-answer-with-a-web search questions.

cues.zh: 我自己甚至也被人这样回过一次。
cues.en: I was even on the receiving end of that once.

cues.zh: 但我想谈的并不完全是这个。
cues.en: But that’s not quite what I want to talk about.

cues.zh: 我想谈谈我们如何决定自己在互联网上想看什么、看什么、做什么。
cues.en: I want to talk about how we decide what we want to see, watch, and do on the internet.

cues.zh: 因为，嗯，我不确定我们是否意识到，如今我们真正自己做决定的频率有多低。
cues.en: Because, well, I’m not sure we realize just how infrequently we’re actually deciding for ourselves these days.

cues.zh: 没错，这期视频讲的是社交媒体乃至整个互联网上推荐算法带来的问题。
cues.en: That’s right, this is video about the problems of recommendation algorithms on social media and the internet at large.

cues.zh: 但我不会过多关注这些算法具体在做什么。我想现在大家应该都知道了。
cues.en: But I’m not gonna be focusing much on what exactly those algorithms do. I think we all know by now.

cues.zh: 相反，我要关注的是某种让人感觉新奇又不安的东西。
cues.en: Instead I’m going to be focusing on something which feels new and troubling.

cues.zh: 我开始看到证据表明，越来越多的人实际上更愿意让计算机程序决定他们登录后会看到什么，
cues.en: I’m starting to see evidence that an increasing number of folks actually prefer to let a computer program decide what they will see when they log on,

cues.zh: 即使他们知道自己有别的选择。
cues.en: even when they know they have alternatives.

cues.zh: 既然这感觉像是个新现象，我觉得它需要一个名字。
cues.en: Since this feels like a new phenomenon, I felt it needed a name.

cues.zh: 我选择称之为“算法自满”。
cues.en: I’ve chosen to call it “algorithmic complacency.”

cues.zh: 我明白，我正踏入一场许多人都讨论过的对话，
cues.en: Now, I recognize that I am stepping into a discussion that many many people have had

cues.zh: 所以我不想声称这是什么原创想法，甚至不是原创术语。
cues.en: and so I don’t want to claim that this is an original thought or even an original term.

cues.zh: 但在我努力定义和阐述它的过程中，我逐渐相信这是一个需要立即关注的严重问题。
cues.en: But as I’ve worked to define and articulate it, I’ve come to believe that it’s a serious problem that needs our immediate attention.

cues.zh: 屈服于算法带来的自满，意味着你在不知不觉中放弃了自己的自主权。
cues.en: Succumbing to algorithmic complacency means you’re surrendering your own agency in ways you may not realize.

cues.zh: 随着互联网和现实生活不断融合，后果可能非常糟糕。
cues.en: And as the internet and real life continue to blend together, that can end very badly.

cues.zh: 我认为这个话题分量很重，所以想给你们一个有力的论证。
cues.en: Since I believe there’s significant gravity to this topic, I want to present a convincing argument to you.

cues.zh: 而这需要我们首先回顾一下过去。
cues.en: And that requires that we first look backward in time.

cues.zh: 想一想你如今上网的体验是什么样的，如果你年纪够大，再想想它和二十年前有什么不同。
cues.en: Think for a moment about what your experience on the internet is like these days and, if you’re old enough, how it differs from a couple of decades ago.

cues.zh: 互联网曾经只存在于台式电脑的网页浏览器里。
cues.en: The internet used to only exist through a web browser on a desktop computer.

cues.zh: 如果你讲究点，也许是笔记本电脑。
cues.en: Maybe a laptop if you’re fancy.

cues.zh: [背景中有拨号音和拨号声] 而且你的电脑得假装成电话，通过电话线对其他电脑尖叫
cues.en: [dial tone and dialing in background] And your computer had to pretend to be a telephone and shriek at other computers through a phone line

cues.zh: 只为了以极慢的速度收发数据。
cues.en: just to transmit and receive data at blazing slow speeds.

cues.zh: 那是一个黑暗的时期。
cues.en: It was a dark time.

cues.zh: 那时，Google 还只是一个快乐的搜索引擎，帮你找到各种网站，
cues.en: Back then, Google was just a happy little search engine which helped you find websites,

cues.zh: 当你发现一个喜欢的酷网站时，你会用浏览器把它收藏起来。
cues.en: and when you found a cool website which you liked you’d use your web browser to bookmark that website.

cues.zh: 这样就能确保你以后不用再搜索就能回到那个网站。
cues.en: That would make sure you could get back to it later without having to search for it again.

cues.zh: 就像给自己写个便条一样。
cues.en: Like writing a note to yourself.

cues.zh: 换句话说，那时的互联网还非常手动化，你得自己导航，自己策划自己的使用体验。
cues.en: In other words, the internet was still very manual and you were in charge of navigating it and curating your own experience with it.

cues.zh: 这也意味着，互联网不会主动做任何事，直到你让它做。
cues.en: That also meant the internet didn’t do anything until you asked it to do something.

cues.zh: 你可能会把浏览器主页设成本地报纸的网站，这样每次上网时就能顺便看看新闻更新，
cues.en: You might set your browser’s homepage to your local newspaper’s website so you could get a bit of a news update each time you logged on

cues.zh: 但除此之外，信息并不会主动来找你。
cues.en: but other than that, information didn’t just come to you.

cues.zh: 过去，在互联网上找新闻、产品和信息，完全靠你自己。
cues.en: Finding news, products, and information on the internet was entirely up to you.

cues.zh: 世界的信息就在你指尖，但你得动手指、动脑子才能找到。
cues.en: You had the world’s information at your fingertips, but you needed to use your fingertips and your brain to get to it.

cues.zh: 而且，信息是否可信可靠，也得你自己判断。
cues.en: And it was also up to you to gauge the trustworthiness and reliability of the information you found.

cues.zh: 如果你超过30岁，大概还记得那是什么感觉。
cues.en: If you’re over the age of 30 you probably remember what this was like.

cues.zh: 但久而久之，这一切逐渐变得自动化多了。
cues.en: Overtime, though, things have steadily become a lot more automated.

cues.zh: 也变得更加扑面而来。
cues.en: And also a lot more in-your-face.

cues.zh: 如今很多人主要通过智能手机和移动应用上网，
cues.en: Many people these days experience the internet primarily through their smartphones and mobile apps

cues.zh: 身处科技巨头打造和精心策划的、包装精美的生态系统中。
cues.en: in a neatly-packaged ecosystem created and curated by giant tech corporations.

cues.zh: 尽管这些应用往往只是定制的网页浏览器，只把你带到某个特定网站，把你的流量困在围墙花园里，
cues.en: Even though those apps are often just bespoke web browsers that only take you to a very specific website and keep your traffic inside a walled garden

cues.zh: 同时大量收集你去过哪里、做了什么的各类数据，
cues.en: while also collecting lots of data about where you go and what you do,

cues.zh: 它们仍然代表着我们作为资源使用和体验互联网的方式发生了根本性转变。
cues.en: they still represent a radical shift in how we use and experience the internet as a resource.

cues.zh: 平台成了新的游戏规则。
cues.en: Platforms became the new name of the game.

cues.zh: 我们不再上网搜寻酷炫实用的东西，而是泡在平台上。
cues.en: We’re not surfing the web and looking for cool and useful things anymore, we’re hanging out on platforms.

cues.zh: 比如，这个平台。
cues.en: Like, well, this one.

cues.zh: 我们已经太习惯了，以至于不再把应用看作连接人与信息的软件，
cues.en: We’re so used to this now that we imagine apps less as a piece of software which enables connection to people and information

cues.zh: 而更像是一个我们消磨时间的地方。
cues.en: and more of a place where we spend time.

cues.zh: 互联网历史学家提醒我们，这可不是我们第一次经历这种事。毕竟我们逃离过AOL的围墙花园。
cues.en: Internet historians remind us that this is not our first rodeo. We escaped the walled garden that was AOL, after all.

cues.zh: 但我认为多数人会同意，今天的互联网截然不同，而且强度更高。
cues.en: But I think most would agree that today’s internet is distinctly different and intense.

cues.zh: 它已深度融入我们的生活，正在塑造我们看待世界的方式，以及我们在其中行事的方式。
cues.en: It has become so integral to our lives that it’s shaping how we view the world and how we operate within it.

cues.zh: 最令人不安的是，我们看到什么，很大程度上已不再由我们掌控。
cues.en: And most troublingly, we are largely no longer in control of what we see.

cues.zh: 推荐算法最终把内容推到我们眼前，用的方法几乎没人真正理解
cues.en: Recommendation algorithms end up putting content in front of our eyes using methods almost nobody really understands

cues.zh: （但大概和最大化收入有关），
cues.en: (but probably have something to do with maximizing revenues) and,

cues.zh: 嗯，我觉得这正在摧毁我们的大脑。
cues.en: well, I think it’s breaking our brains.

cues.zh: 当那条经过精细调校、算法量身定制的信息消防水管就这样朝你喷涌而来，
cues.en: When you have that finely-tuned, algorithmically-tailored firehose of information just coming at you like that,

cues.zh: 你可能觉得自己玩得挺开心，还学到了一些有趣的东西，
cues.en: you might feel like you’re having a good time and learning some interesting things,

cues.zh: 但你未必在主导自己的体验，对吧？
cues.en: but you’re not necessarily directing your own experience, are you?

cues.zh: 当下一次滑动就可能让你的思路脱轨时，你的思绪真的还是你自己的吗？
cues.en: Is your train of thought really your own when the next swipe might derail it?

cues.zh: 我绝不是第一个提出这个问题的人。
cues.en: Now, I am by no means the first person to ask that question.

cues.zh: 而且，坦白说，我靠寻找信息、把它包装成我希望既有娱乐性又有洞见的视频来谋生，
cues.en: And, full disclosure, I make my living finding information, packaging it into videos which I hope are entertaining and insightful,

cues.zh: 再把它们放到网上，希望人们在YouTube算法推荐时偶然刷到。
cues.en: and putting them online for people to hopefully stumble across when the YouTube algorithm recommends it to them.

cues.zh: 我明白，这个特定的人在这个特定的平台上谈论这件特定的事，确实有些尴尬。
cues.en: So I recognize the awkwardness of this particular person talking about this particular thing on this particular platform.

cues.zh: 但我认为可能有些新东西，或者至少是讨论不足的地方：
cues.en: But here’s what I think might be new, or at least under-discussed:

cues.zh: 我看到越来越多的证据表明，越来越多的人已经太习惯算法生成的推送流，
cues.en: I am seeing mounting evidence that an increasing number of people are so used to algorithmically-generated feeds

cues.zh: 以至于他们不再在意拥有一个由自己掌控、自主导向的体验。
cues.en: that they no longer care to have a self-directed experience that they are in control of.

cues.zh: 我在网上与人互动的时间越长，就越觉得一大群人似乎已经忘了如何行使自己的自主权。
cues.en: The more time I spend interacting with folks online, the more it feels like large swaths of people have forgotten to exercise their own agency.

cues.zh: 这就是我所说的算法惰性。
cues.en: That is what I mean by algorithmic complacency.

cues.zh: 越来越多的人似乎不知道、也不在乎如何在没有计算机算法引导所见内容的情况下去看世界。
cues.en: More and more people don’t seem to know or care how to view the world without a computer algorithm guiding what they see.

cues.zh: 我刚才提出了一个相当大胆的论断，这需要证据来支撑。
cues.en: That’s a pretty bold claim I just made, and that’s gonna require evidence.

cues.zh: 我先说明，我的证据并不科学，所以请相应调整预期。
cues.en: I will say up front that my evidence is not scientific, so set your expectations accordingly.

cues.zh: 我确实有某一方面的数据，但我想稍后再谈那个。
cues.en: I do have data for one particular thing but I want to talk about that second.

cues.zh: 首先，我想谈谈我在新型社交媒体上的经历，以及这如何影响了我的论点。
cues.en: First, I want to talk about my experiences on new forms of social media and how that has informed this argument.

cues.zh: 我早就放弃了“传统？”社交媒体
cues.en: I have long given up on “traditional?” social media

cues.zh: 但我一直在尝试一些替代品，比如Mastodon，以及最近的Bluesky。
cues.en: but I’ve been indulging in some of the alternatives like Mastodon and, lately, Bluesky.

cues.zh: 需要说明的是，我并不是在推销让你使用它们，
cues.en: I’m not trying to sell you on using them, to be clear,

cues.zh: 但这两个平台比Meta或Twitter之流可能搞出来的任何东西都要手动得多。
cues.en: but both of those platforms are far more manual than anything the likes of Meta or Twitter might have spun up.

cues.zh: 我觉得这很棒，相当令人耳目一新！
cues.en: I think this is great and quite refreshing!

cues.zh: 我关注我感兴趣的账号，而且从不用担心算法会不会不给我看他们的帖子。
cues.en: I follow accounts that I’m interested in, and I never have to worry about whether an algorithm won’t show me their posts.

cues.zh: 我一直在发现新账号，但都是通过我关注的人分享的内容。
cues.en: I still discover new accounts all the time, but through stuff the ones I’m following have shared.

cues.zh: 这比让算法决定把什么东西推到我眼前要人性化得多
cues.en: That’s a much more human experience than letting an algorithm decide to put stuff in front of my eyeballs

cues.zh: 因为算法会让我保持参与度，增加我在平台上的使用时间。
cues.en: because it will keep me engaged and increase user time on platform.

cues.zh: 这也是一种更具社交性的体验。
cues.en: It’s also a much more social experience.

cues.zh: 然而对许多正在迁移到这些平台的新用户来说，需要自己策划体验这件事非常令人沮丧。
cues.en: Yet to a lot of new users that are migrating to these platforms, the need to curate your own experience is very frustrating.

cues.zh: 其中几个人直接跟我说过这一点，甚至说他们希望不用在社交媒体上投入任何精力。
cues.en: Several of whom have told me this directly and even said they’d prefer not to have to put any work into social media.

cues.zh: 现在，我必须承认，光是这种情绪就让我感到担忧。
cues.en: Now, I must admit that sentiment alone concerns me.

cues.zh: 我就是那种怪人，认为生活中最有回报的事情需要付出努力，
cues.en: I’m one of those weirdos who think the most rewarding things in life take effort,

cues.zh: 至少十一月之外是这样，
cues.en: at least outside November,

cues.zh: 所以我不会指望刚走进一个新地方就能玩得开心，而不做一点老派的探索。
cues.en: so I would not expect to just walk into a new place and have a good time without doing a little ol’ fashioned exploring.

cues.zh: 不过，我能理解这种感受。
cues.en: However, I can sympathize with it.

cues.zh: 首先，我得承认自己是个受欢迎的YouTuber，随便出现在某个地方，说一句“大家好”
cues.en: For one, I have to recognize that I’m a popular YouTuber and I can just show up somewhere, say “hey guys”

cues.zh: 就能指望很多人迅速开始关注我，这也帮我重新建立了在其他地方形成的人脉。
cues.en: and expect a lot of people to start following me very quickly, and that helped re-establish connections I formed in other places.

cues.zh: 这是我拥有的一种特权，很大程度上扭曲了我的视角，我理应承认这一点。
cues.en: That’s a privilege I have and skews my perspective a lot, which is only fair that I acknowledge.

cues.zh: 我在网上的经历并不正常。
cues.en: My experience online is not normal.

cues.zh: 但观察Bluesky从一个极其小众的平台成长为一个仍然小众但快速增长的平台
cues.en: But observing Bluesky grow from an extremely niche platform to a still-niche-but-quickly-growing one

cues.zh: 呈现了一个非常有趣的案例，我觉得有必要分享出来。
cues.en: has presented a very interesting case study which I feel compelled to share.

cues.zh: 可能有人不知道，Bluesky允许创建自定义信息流。
cues.en: Bluesky, for those who don’t know, allows for the creation of custom feeds.

cues.zh: 这是它的核心功能之一，真的很酷！
cues.en: That’s one of its central features which is really cool!

cues.zh: 但创建账户时，默认内置了两个用途不同的信息流：
cues.en: But baked-into it as a default when you create an account are two feeds with different purposes:

cues.zh: 关注和发现。
cues.en: Following and Discover.

cues.zh: 关注信息流是按时间倒序排列的，显示你关注的账户发布的帖子。
cues.en: The Following feed is a reverse-chronological feed of the posts from accounts you follow.

cues.zh: 就像Twitter以前那样。
cues.en: Exactly how Twitter used to work.

cues.zh: 但发现信息流是算法驱动的，就像大家都在说的那些“为你推荐”页面。
cues.en: But the Discover feed is algorithmic, like those “for you” pages everyone keeps going on about.

cues.zh: 在Bluesky上，它的算法相当基础，
cues.en: On Bluesky it’s a pretty basic algorithm,

cues.zh: 但它的作用是从平台上各个账户中挑选帖子，本质上就是推广它们，让人们能找到新的账户来关注。
cues.en: but its job is to pick posts from accounts across the platform and essentially promote them so people can find new accounts to follow.

cues.zh: 有这个功能绝不是坏主意！
cues.en: It’s by no means a bad idea to have that feature!

cues.zh: 但作为一个在Bluesky上粉丝相当多的人，
cues.en: But as someone with a pretty large following on Bluesky now,

cues.zh: 我能立刻知道我的帖子什么时候上了发现信息流，因为回复会很快变得非常奇怪。
cues.en: I can tell the instant a post of mine ends up on the discover feed because the replies get real weird real fast.

cues.zh: 以前一条帖子下面会有我和各种认识我、也懂我话里意思的人展开的良性讨论
cues.en: What was previously a post with a nice discussion going on underneath between myself and various people who know who I am and what I mean when I say words

cues.zh: 现在却被一堆莫名其妙的、断章取义的、往往还带敌意的回复刷满
cues.en: becomes littered with strange, out-of-context, often antagonistic replies

cues.zh: 就好像在网上看到任何一条帖子，唯一可能的反应就是大声地对着它叫板。
cues.en: as if the only possible response to seeing a post of any kind online is to loudly perform a challenge against it.

cues.zh: 其中有些是机器人，这是 Bluesky 上众所周知的问题。
cues.en: Now, some of these are bots, a known problem on Bluesky.

cues.zh: 但因为我养成了回复前先看主页、判断有没有机器人迹象的习惯，很明显其中很多并不是机器人。
cues.en: But through forming a habit where I check profiles before replying to see if they show signs of being a bot, it’s clear that a lot of them are not.

cues.zh: 他们就是些开口就说话的人，完全不知道自己在跟谁说话，也根本不想在回复前搞清楚讨论的来龙去脉。
cues.en: They’re people who just start talking with absolutely no idea who they’re talking to and with no desire to figure out the context of the discussion before they write their reply.

cues.zh: 这可能感觉我有点跑题了，或者只是在吐槽别人，不过这挺有意思的，
cues.en: This may feel like I’m veering off track a bit or just complaining about people, which is fun,

cues.zh: 但这不是在指责个人的行为，而是要认识到助长这种行为背后的激励机制。
cues.en: but this is less about calling out the behavior of individuals and more about recognizing the incentives which promote that behavior.

cues.zh: 不幸的是，社交媒体上的算法信息流非常擅长培养一种叫做语境坍塌的现象。
cues.en: Algorithmic feeds on social media are unfortunately quite good at fostering something known as context collapse.

cues.zh: 要理解这一点，想象你在餐厅用餐，你离一桌人很近，能听到他们谈话的片段。
cues.en: To understand this, imagine you’re dining in a restaurant and you’re close enough to a table of people to hear snippets of their conversation.

cues.zh: 你不知道那桌人是谁，
cues.en: You don’t know who any of the people at that table are,

cues.zh: 但如果你碰巧听到他们在聊你非常感兴趣的话题，你可能会忍不住想加入他们的对话。
cues.en: but if you manage to overhear them talk about something you’re really interested in you might feel tempted to join their conversation.

cues.zh: 但在餐厅这个场景下，那样做会被认为非常无礼，所以很少会发生。
cues.en: But in the context of a restaurant setting, that’s considered very rude so it rarely ever happens.

cues.zh: 但在社交媒体上，熟人之间那种半私密的对话时时刻刻都在发生，
cues.en: On social media, though, the same kinds of quasi-private conversations between parties who know each other are happening all the time,

cues.zh: 但既然平台就是一个大空间，它可能决定把那段对话推给随便什么人看，
cues.en: but since the platform is just one big space and it might decide to put that conversation in front of random people,

cues.zh: 那条本该被遵守的社交礼仪边界就不存在了。
cues.en: that social boundary of etiquette which is normally respected is just not there.

cues.zh: 结果就会产生大量冲突。
cues.en: And lots of conflicts happen as a result.

cues.zh: 有一种很常见的情况，你可能在社交媒体上无意间就卷进去了，
cues.en: A really common one you might accidentally step into on social media

cues.zh: 就是当你偶然看到朋友之间互相开讽刺玩笑的对话，
cues.en: happens when you stumble across a conversation among friends making sarcastic jokes with each other

cues.zh: 但你不认识那些人，所以你没有足够的背景信息去意识到他们在开玩笑。
cues.en: but since you don’t know who those people are you don’t have the context you need to recognize they’re joking.

cues.zh: 于是，如果你一本正经地回复批评，那就是一次社交失误，有些人会反应很差。
cues.en: And so, if you reply with a serious critique, well that’s a social misfire which some will react poorly to.

cues.zh: 而这还只是上下文坍缩中相当温和的一种形式。
cues.en: And that’s a pretty mild form of context collapse.

cues.zh: 当人们想讨论政治之类的话题时，情况会糟糕得多。
cues.en: It can be much, much worse when people want to discuss things like politics.

cues.zh: 除非我们意识到推荐算法正是助长这些反动冲突的推手，
cues.en: And unless we realize recommendation algorithms are what’s fostering these reactionary conflicts,

cues.zh: 否则只要我们继续以现在的方式使用平台，它们就会持续下去。
cues.en: they’re going to continue so long as we use platforms in the ways that we do.

cues.zh: 正是出于这些原因，我相信算法带来的自满正在制造一场好奇心和人际连接的危机。
cues.en: It's for all these reasons that I believe algorithmic complacency is creating a crisis of both curiosity and human connection.

cues.zh: 我甚至要说，它还在助长许多其他令人不安的东西。
cues.en: I would even go so far as to say it’s fostering lots of other disturbing things, too.

cues.zh: 有没有注意到，如今很多人对某个话题或议题，非得要有一个简单的
cues.en: Ever notice how a lot of folks these days need to have a simple

cues.zh: “好或坏”、
cues.en: “good or bad,”

cues.zh: “黑或白”、
cues.en: “black or white,”

cues.zh: “最好或最差”的理解？
cues.en: “best or worst” understanding of a topic or issue?

cues.zh: 在我看来，算法通过正面或负面互动的简单视角来推广内容，
cues.en: It seems to me like algorithms which promote content through a simple lens of positive or negative engagement

cues.zh: 会强化这些二元对立，加剧极化。
cues.en: would reinforce those binaries and contribute to polarization.

cues.zh: 人们通过社交媒体信息流的老虎机式推送来了解新产品，
cues.en: And as people learn about new products through the slot machine of social media feeds,

cues.zh: 就会形成习得性无助，等着别人来推销解决自己问题的方案，
cues.en: they can develop a learned helplessness where they will wait to be sold on a solution for their problems

cues.zh: 而不是内省，去探究自己的问题究竟是什么，以及如何自己想出不花钱的解决办法。
cues.en: rather than be introspective and explore what their problems actually are and how they might be able to come up with their own solutions which don’t cost any money.

cues.zh: 内省会发现，你以为自己有的很多问题，其实是网红塞进你脑子里的——
cues.en: Introspection will reveal a lot of the problems you think you have are being put in your head by influencers -

cues.zh: 在他们告诉你应该不快乐之前，你本来并不不快乐。
cues.en: you weren’t unhappy until they told you you should be.

cues.zh: 而且，我能想到很多其他事情，它们困扰我相当长一段时间了，
cues.en: And, well, I can think of lots of other stuff which has disturbed me for quite a while

cues.zh: 但现在已经到了无法再忽视的地步，不能再把它们当作把大量人类连接在一起的古怪副作用了。
cues.en: but is now past the point I can ignore as a quirky consequence of connecting large numbers of humans together.

cues.zh: 社交媒体算法不是在培育人际连接，而是在利用它。
cues.en: Social media algorithms don’t nurture human connection - they exploit it.

cues.zh: 我们如今太习惯这种现实了，我不确定还有多少人愿意下这趟车。
cues.en: And we’re so used to this reality now that I’m not sure many of us care to get off this train.

cues.zh: 但我觉得我们应该下车。
cues.en: But I think we should.

cues.zh: 那么现在，我们来聊聊YouTube！
cues.en: So now, let’s talk about YouTube!

cues.zh: 我相信你们不少人会想：“这话从一个靠这个平台谋生的人嘴里说出来，可真是讽刺。”
cues.en: I’m sure a good number of you have thought “this is pretty rich comin’ from a guy who makes his living on a platform which does all these things.”

cues.zh: 不过，YouTube有个有趣的地方。
cues.en: Well, there’s a funny thing about YouTube.

cues.zh: 它的推荐算法完全是可选的。
cues.en: Its recommendation algorithm is entirely optional.

cues.zh: 你们知道的，对吧？
cues.en: You know that, right?

cues.zh: 你们……你们确实知道吧？
cues.en: You… you do know that, right?

cues.zh: 这个网站上有个功能，几乎从它诞生起就存在了，叫做订阅动态。
cues.en: There’s this feature on this website that has been here pretty much since it became a thing and it’s called the subscriptions feed.

cues.zh: 它没藏起来，就在移动应用底部和桌面网站的侧边栏里。
cues.en: It’s not hiding, it’s at the bottom of the mobile app and on the sidebar of the desktop site.

cues.zh: 事实上它有自己的 URL，如果你喜欢老派做法，还可以把它加进书签！
cues.en: In fact it's got its own URL and if you’re feeling old-school you can bookmark it!

cues.zh: 这是一个完全人工精选的信息流，里面只有视频
cues.en: This is a completely manually-curated feed which has nothing in it but the videos

cues.zh: （还有短视频，好坏参半）全都来自你选择订阅的创作者。
cues.en: (and shorts, for better and worse) from the creators you have chosen to subscribe to.

cues.zh: 这意味着它完全由你掌控。
cues.en: That means it’s entirely in your control.

cues.zh: 这个信息流一直都明摆在那里，而我之所以用“算法自满”这个词，
cues.en: This feed has been in plain sight the whole time and, here’s why I am using the term algorithmic complacency,

cues.zh: 是因为没人愿意去用它。
cues.en: nobody cares to use it.

cues.zh: 这一点我可以用硬数据来佐证。
cues.en: And that I can back up with hard data.

cues.zh: YouTube 给了我们多得惊人的受众指标信息，而在 2024 年，
cues.en: YouTube gives us a shocking amount of information regarding audience metrics and in 2024,

cues.zh: 这个频道不到 3% 的观看量来自订阅信息流。
cues.en: less than three percent of this channel’s views came from the subscriptions feed.

cues.zh: 几乎没人在用这个功能
cues.en: Almost nobody is using this feature

cues.zh: 可它却是追踪你通过点击订阅按钮、明确决定要观看的内容最可靠的方式。
cues.en: and yet it’s the most reliable way to keep track of the things you have explicitly decided you want to watch through hitting the subscribe button.

cues.zh: 这件事很容易做到，几乎从这个平台诞生起就一直明摆在那儿，却几乎没人再用了，这真是……
cues.en: The fact that it’s easy to get to, has existed in plain sight almost since this platform was born, yet almost nobody is using it anymore is…

cues.zh: 令人费解。
cues.en: puzzling.

cues.zh: 我想强调一下我用“令人费解”这个词的分量。
cues.en: I want to stress my use of the word puzzling.

cues.zh: 我无意在这里做评判，如果听起来像那样，我很抱歉。
cues.en: It’s not my intent to be judgmental here and I’m sorry if it has sounded like that.

cues.zh: 不同的人使用网站的方式不同，而 YouTube 上主要的“首页”信息流，功能就像一个“为你推荐”页面，
cues.en: Different people use websites differently and the main “home” feed on YouTube, which functions like a “for-you” page,

cues.zh: 通常能很好地推送你喜欢的创作者的新视频。
cues.en: usually does a good job of surfacing new videos from creators you like.

cues.zh: 订阅一个频道，就是向推荐算法发出信号，让它在你首页信息流中提升该频道视频的权重。
cues.en: Subscribing to a channel is a signal to the recommendation algorithm to boost that channel’s videos in your home feed.

cues.zh: 而且这个算法并非毫无价值——有些创作者我甚至都没订阅，
cues.en: And it’s not like that algorithm has no value - there are some creators I’m not even subscribed to

cues.zh: 但我能看到他们的大部分新视频，因为算法已经搞明白我一直在看他们的内容，所以我肯定想看新的，于是就把它们放进了我的首页信息流。
cues.en: yet I see most of their new videos since the algorithm has figured out I keep watching them so I must want to see the new ones, and it puts them in my home feed.

cues.zh: 通过这个订阅源，我还偶然发现了无数新频道，也重新想起了多年前看过、现在依然乐意再看一遍的视频。
cues.en: Through that feed I’ve also stumbled across countless new channels and have been reminded of videos I watched years ago and will happily watch again.

cues.zh: 当然，我还通过伴随我正在观看的视频出现的推荐内容，发现了太多很酷的东西。
cues.en: Plus of course, I have found so much cool stuff through the recommended videos that appear alongside whatever I happen to be watching.

cues.zh: 我很高兴YouTube这么做。
cues.en: I’m glad YouTube does that.

cues.zh: 等等，细微差别？
cues.en: Wait, nuance?

cues.zh: 在互联网上？
cues.en: On the internet?

cues.zh: 那可是违法的！
cues.en: That’s illegal!

cues.zh: 为了节省时间，我删掉了一大段关于订阅源缺陷以及我认为YouTube应如何解决这些问题的内容
cues.en: In the interest of time I’ve removed a big section on the flaws with the subs feed and how I think YouTube should address them

cues.zh: （主要是——请让我们能移除不感兴趣的Shorts
cues.en: (mainly - please let us remove shorts if we aren’t interested in them

cues.zh: 并且请让我们能稍微整理一下订阅源，这样上传频繁的创作者就不会把订阅源弄得杂乱不堪。
cues.en: and please lets us organize the subs feed a little bit so creators who upload a lot don’t end up cluttering it.

cues.zh: 也许可以把他们每天的活动浓缩成一个单独的卡片，我们可以点击展开。只是个小建议。）
cues.en: Maybe condense their daily activity into a single tile which we can then click on and expand. Just a thought).

cues.zh: 但我想聊这个的原因是
cues.en: But the reason I wanted to talk about it

cues.zh: 它似乎反映出一种日益增长的不情愿——不愿去握住互联网的缰绳，不愿做那个掌控自身体验的人。
cues.en: is that it feels indicative of a growing disinclination to grab the reins of the internet and be the person steering your own experience.

cues.zh: 这才是真正让我不安的地方。
cues.en: That’s really what bothers me.

cues.zh: 在偶然发现的酷东西和你真正感兴趣、真正在意的东西之间，必须有一种平衡。
cues.en: There has to be a balance between cool stuff you stumble upon and stuff that you’re actually interested in and matters to you.

cues.zh: 算法带来的自满，如果不被察觉并采取行动，
cues.en: Algorithmic complacency, if not noticed and acted upon,

cues.zh: 就意味着你在允许那些不是你的人来决定什么对你重要。
cues.en: means you’re allowing other people who are not you to decide what matters to you.

cues.zh: 这本不必我解释为什么这很危险，所以我就不多说了。
cues.en: I should not have to spell out why that’s dangerous so I won’t.

cues.zh: 但我要说明的是，那些想把这个现实武器化的人，很容易就能编造出一套并不显眼的叙事，从而悄悄越过你的防线。
cues.en: But I will spell out that it’s very easy for people who wish to weaponize this reality to craft a narrative which is not overtly obvious and so might slip past your defenses.

cues.zh: 如果你能减少生活中算法推荐内容的存在，你就不会那么容易受其影响。
cues.en: If you can reduce the presence of algorithmically-curated feeds in your life, you’ll be less susceptible to that.

cues.zh: 如果你建立起自己信任的人脉和资源网络，你就能分辨出什么时候有人在忽悠你。
cues.en: And if you build up your own network of people and resources you trust, you’ll know when you’re being bullshitted.

cues.zh: 你可能还没注意到，现在人们无时无刻不在试图忽悠我们！
cues.en: And in case you haven’t noticed, people are trying to bullshit us all the time now!

cues.zh: 而算法推荐让这种情况更糟。
cues.en: And algorithmic feeds make this worse.

cues.zh: 它们不仅存在于YouTube和社交媒体上，还存在于流行的新闻聚合应用里，这意味着很多非常愚蠢的文章一直在流传
cues.en: They don’t just exist on YouTube and social media, they exist in popular news aggregator apps and that’s meant a lot of really stupid articles keep floating around

cues.zh: 因为对如今很多做新闻的机构来说，唯一重要的就是点击量和广告收入。
cues.en: because all that matters to many institutions which make news these days is clicks and ad money.

cues.zh: 看看这个蠢东西，它居然出现在了Google News应用里。
cues.en: Look at this stupid thing which ended up in the Google News app.

cues.zh: “沃尔玛和塔吉特在美国的终结——一家新零售商出现，而且便宜得多。”
cues.en: "The end of Walmart and Target in the US - A new retailer appears and is much cheaper."

cues.zh: 我知道Aldi长什么样。
cues.en: I know what an Aldi looks like.

cues.zh: 这是Aldi内部的照片。
cues.en: That’s a picture of the inside of an Aldi.

cues.zh: 而且，呃，如果你不知怎么地没听说过Aldi，或者没走进过一家Aldi，那并不意味着Aldi是一个刚刚出现的新零售商。
cues.en: And, uh, if you’ve somehow not heard of Aldi or stepped inside one that doesn’t mean Aldi is a new retailer which just appeared.

cues.zh: 这篇文章对绝大多数可能被诱骗点击的人来说是浪费时间。
cues.en: This article is a waste of time for the vast majority of people who might be tricked into clicking on it.

cues.zh: 你可能注意到了，那篇文章的发布者是El Diario 24，据我所知，它实际上可能是一个假新闻来源。
cues.en: You may have noticed that the publisher of that article was El Diario 24 which, as far as I can tell, might actually be a fake news source.

cues.zh: 它是怎么进入Google News的？
cues.en: How did it get in Google News?

cues.zh: 这对Google来说是个好问题。
cues.en: That’s a great question for Google.

cues.zh: 但即使是主流出版物，在追逐指标而非真相的过程中也完全失控了。
cues.en: But even mainstream publications have gone wildly off the rails as they chase metrics rather than the truth.

cues.zh: 2025年的《纽约时报》正在发表观点文章，
cues.en: The New York Times of 2025 is publishing opinion pieces

cues.zh: 其中那些夸夸其谈的蠢货们在做一个有趣的小练习：把加拿大变成第51个州对民主党会有什么政治影响。
cues.en: where bloviating morons go through the fun little exercise of what the political ramifications of turning Canada into the 51st state would be for Democrats.

cues.zh: 各位，既然他们不知为何不能用大白话说清楚，那只好我来了。
cues.en: Folks, since they can’t say this in plain language for some reason, I guess it’s up to me.

cues.zh: 加拿大是一个主权国家。
cues.en: Canada is a sovereign nation.

cues.zh: 它是一个拥有自决权的外国。
cues.en: It’s a foreign country which has the right to self-determination.

cues.zh: 美国不能就这么把加拿大变成美国的一个州——
cues.en: The United States cannot simply turn Canada into a US state -

cues.zh: 加拿大人已经明确表示他们不想这样，
cues.en: Canadians have clearly indicated they do not want that,

cues.zh: 这意味着我们若强行推动，就等于向加拿大宣战并入侵。
cues.en: which means for us to force the issue would be to declare war with Canada and invade.

cues.zh: 任何理智的人都不该想要那样，
cues.en: No sane person should want that

cues.zh: 而《纽约时报》竟然把这种事当作一种可能性来讨论，还让这个糟糕透顶、必然血腥的想法显得正当，这真是丢人现眼。
cues.en: and it’s a shameful embarrassment that the New York Times would even entertain this as a possibility and legitimize the awful, inevitably bloody idea.

cues.zh: 我们到底是怎么走到这一步的？
cues.en: How on Earth did we get here?

cues.zh: 我可以告诉你们我认为我们是怎么走到这一步的：
cues.en: I can tell you how I think we got here:

cues.zh: 大型新闻出版物如今依赖算法来找到读者，程度不亚于读者依赖算法来找到新闻。
cues.en: big news publications have become just as dependent on algorithms to find their readers as their readers are to find the news.

cues.zh: 也就是说，它们更在意的是诱人，而不是诚实。
cues.en: Which means they’re more concerned with being enticing than being honest.

cues.zh: 这真是太可惜了。
cues.en: Which is a damn shame.

cues.zh: 好了，收一收。
cues.en: OK, reel it in.

cues.zh: 收一收。
cues.en: Reel it in.

cues.zh: 我准备结束这个视频了，但在结束之前，我想再探讨一个相关但不同的角度。
cues.en: I’m about to wrap up this video but before I do, I want to explore one more related but different angle.

cues.zh: 我纠结过该把这种现象叫作算法自满还是自动化自满。
cues.en: I struggled with whether I wanted to call this phenomenon algorithmic complacency or automation complacency.

cues.zh: 我纠结的原因是，这两者之间并没有明确的界限。
cues.en: The reason I struggled is that there isn’t a clear distinction between those two things.

cues.zh: 算法是一种自动化，所以你可以说我一直讲的一切都是自动策划的信息流带来的结果
cues.en: Algorithms are a kind of automation, so you could say everything I’ve been talking about is the result of automatically-curated feeds

cues.zh: 视频也不会有什么不同。
cues.en: and the video wouldn’t change.

cues.zh: 但自动化本身并不一定是坏事。
cues.en: But automation in itself is not necessarily bad.

cues.zh: 许多琐碎的体力劳动任务已被自动化取代，这在很大程度上是件好事。
cues.en: Lots of menial labor tasks have been replaced by automation and this has largely been a great thing.

cues.zh: 这段讨论中真正重要的词是“策展”。
cues.en: The actually-important word in this discussion is curated.

cues.zh: 自动化某些东西是一回事，比如电梯。
cues.en: It’s one thing to automate, say, an elevator.

cues.zh: 或者库存系统。
cues.en: Or an inventory system.

cues.zh: 或者电话交换机。
cues.en: Or a telephone switchboard.

cues.zh: 但自动化人们看到的信息，完全是另一回事。
cues.en: But it’s a very different thing to automate what information people see.

cues.zh: 有些情况下，这种自动化是必要的。
cues.en: There are situations where that sort of automation is necessary.

cues.zh: 网上存储的信息量在不断增加，
cues.en: There’s an ever-increasing amount of information being stored online,

cues.zh: 所以当你在信息的海洋中寻找特定内容时，光靠关键词是不够的。
cues.en: so when you’re looking for something specific amongst that sea of information, keywords by themselves aren't enough.

cues.zh: 我们一开始做的演示
cues.en: The demonstration we did at the beginning

cues.zh: 依赖于 Google 的搜索算法，从我们给的关键词中判断上下文，从而按与推断上下文的相关性对找到的所有内容进行排序。
cues.en: relied on Google’s search algorithm determining context from the keywords we gave it so it could sort everything it found by relevance to that inferred context.

cues.zh: 而且它通常非常擅长这一点，正如我们所见。
cues.en: And it’s usually really good at that, as we saw.

cues.zh: 但情况并非总是如此。
cues.en: But it’s not always.

cues.zh: 我敢肯定，到现在为止，你已经有过那种非常令人沮丧的经历：Google 抓住了错误的上下文，生成了大量无关的结果，
cues.en: I’m sure by now you’ve had the really frustrating experience of Google latching onto the wrong context and producing a lot of irrelevant results,

cues.zh: 而要让算法重新聚焦到正确的上下文上，可能会极其繁琐。
cues.en: and it can be extremely tedious to refocus the algorithm on the correct context.

cues.zh: 当搜索查询中包含一个有许多同音异义词的单词时，这种情况经常发生。
cues.en: This happens a lot when search queries include a word with many homonyms.

cues.zh: 但我们正在迅速远离这样一种范式：搜索查询会呈现一系列来源供我们查看、引用和验证，
cues.en: But we’re rapidly moving away from a paradigm in which search queries present a list of sources for us to look at, cite and verify,

cues.zh: 而如今正被推向一个新的现实，
cues.en: and are now being pressured into a new reality

cues.zh: 在这个现实中，大型语言模型会综合生成对查询的响应，这些响应在统计上很可能产生有用的输出，
cues.en: where large language models synthesize responses to queries which are statistically likely to produce a useful output

cues.zh: 但它们并不为我们提供可验证信息的来源——
cues.en: but which do not provide us with sources of verifiable information -

cues.zh: 或者至少把它们模糊化到许多人不会去核查的程度。
cues.en: or at least obfuscate them to the point that many people are not going to check them.

cues.zh: 我觉得我们中很少有人认真想过这意味着什么。
cues.en: I don’t think enough of us have put much thought into what that means.

cues.zh: 这意味着我们正冲向一个人们完全信任计算机替他们思考的未来。
cues.en: It means we’re careening towards a future where people just trust computers to do their thinking for them.

cues.zh: 而问题是，我们早就知道这往往是个坏主意。
cues.en: And the thing is, we already know that’s often a bad idea.

cues.zh: 就拿我们在现实物理世界中的导航来说吧。
cues.en: Take, for example, how we navigate the actual physical world.

cues.zh: 如果你开车，我敢肯定你到现在一定用过某种GPS导航应用来找到去目的地的路。
cues.en: If you drive a car, I am certain that by now you’ve used some kind of GPS-navigation app to figure out how to get places.

cues.zh: 我也用，别以为我要说“哦我们应该回到纸质地图时代”。
cues.en: I do, too, don’t think I’m about to say "oh we should go back to paper maps."

cues.zh: 太恶心了。
cues.en: Gross.

cues.zh: 但当你用地图应用导航去某地时，你有多经常优先选择最快路线？
cues.en: But when you use a mapping app to navigate somewhere, how often are you prioritizing the fastest route?

cues.zh: 你大概把它设成了默认选项，对吧？
cues.en: You probably have that set up as the default, don’t you?

cues.zh: 我也是。
cues.en: I do.

cues.zh: 但你是否曾质疑过，那真的是到达某地最合乎逻辑的方式吗？
cues.en: But do you ever question whether that is actually the most logical way to get somewhere?

cues.zh: 很多时候并非如此，因为到达时间只是众多可能对你很重要的变量之一。
cues.en: It often isn’t because arrival time is only one of many, many variables which might be important to you.

cues.zh: 如果我让谷歌地图带我從家到办公室，
cues.en: If I ask Google Maps to take me from my home to my office,

cues.zh: 它会建议一条路线，先要绕远路，然后驶入收费公路，我得付大约1美元的过路费，
cues.en: it is going to suggest a route which first requires going the wrong way to then hop on a tollway on which I have to pay a roughly $1 toll

cues.zh: 还得开过目的地，再驶入第二条快速路然后折返。
cues.en: and have to overshoot my destination to hop on a second expressway and backtrack.

cues.zh: 这条建议路线需要多走4英里，单程多花1美元，全都只是为了帮我节省
cues.en: That suggested route requires an extra 4 miles of travel and an extra $1 each way all to save me exactly

cues.zh: 相比走更直接的州道和普通街道，仅仅一分钟的时间。
cues.en: one minute over taking much more direct state routes and surface streets.

cues.zh: 如果我盲目照谷歌的建议去做，
cues.en: If I mindlessly did what Google suggested,

cues.zh: 一年下来，我的车会多跑2000英里，过路费多花500美元，只为省下甚至不到一个完整工作日的时间。
cues.en: over a year I’d put an extra 2,000 miles on my car and spend an extra $500 on tolls just to save not even one full work day of time.

cues.zh: Google建议了一条糟糕的路线，就因为能快一分钟。
cues.en: Google is suggesting a terrible route just because it’s one minute faster.

cues.zh: 我知道这路线糟糕，唯一的原因是我住这儿，我知道它建议的有多蠢，
cues.en: The only reason I know it’s a terrible route is because I live here and I know what it’s suggesting is asinine,

cues.zh: 但当我不知道路怎么走时，我就信它能做出最佳决定。
cues.en: but when I don’t know where I’m going I trust it to make the best decision.

cues.zh: 可我们对“最佳”未必看法一致。
cues.en: But we don’t necessarily agree on what is best.

cues.zh: 问题就在这儿。
cues.en: That’s the problem.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，走收费公路另一个不好的地方是，
cues.en: Side-note, the other bad thing about taking the tollway is that when I do,

cues.zh: 我就看不到我的邻居们，看不到他们在忙啥。
cues.en: I don’t get to see my neighbors and what they’re up to.

cues.zh: 其实我真的很喜欢开车穿过小镇，
cues.en: I actually really enjoy driving through town,

cues.zh: 看着新店铺冒出来，
cues.en: seeing new businesses as they pop up,

cues.zh: 房子建起来、翻新，
cues.en: homes getting built and remodeled,

cues.zh: 节日期间欣赏圣诞灯饰，还有
cues.en: admiring Christmas lights over the holidays, and

cues.zh: 就是看看人，提醒我别人也存在，他们过着真实的生活，他们和我有联系，因为他们是我的邻居。
cues.en: just seeing people to remind me that other people exist and they live real lives and they are connected to me because they’re my neighbors.

cues.zh: 我不是最擅长社交的人
cues.en: I’m not the most social person

cues.zh: 但就连我也不喜欢那种孤立感——在收费公路上通勤，除了别的车和隔音墙，什么也看不到。
cues.en: but even I don’t like the isolated feeling that a commute on a tollway where there’s nothing to look at but other cars and sound-isolation walls gives me.

cues.zh: 当我能真正看到我的社区，看到那些定义它的人时，我会觉得自己与社区的联系紧密得多。
cues.en: I feel way more connected to my community when I can actually, ya know, see it and the people who define it.

cues.zh: 这是我的个人偏好，我承认，但这也是我的优先事项。
cues.en: That’s a preference of mine which I grant but it’s also a priority of mine.

cues.zh: 我现在有意识地要把人与人的连接置于技术连接之上。
cues.en: I am being mindful now to put human connections above technological connections.

cues.zh: 你看，我在这里做的事情，是在各种技术之间建立连接——
cues.en: See, what I do here, is I make connections between technologies -

cues.zh: 这样你就能了解它们如何相互配合、如何最好地使用它们，也许你还能把一个概念和另一个概念结合起来，创造出第三个概念！
cues.en: that way you can learn how they fit together and how best to use them, and maybe you can use one concept in conjunction with another concept to make a third concept!

cues.zh: 这就是我在这里做的事情！
cues.en: That’s what I’m doing here!

cues.zh: 想帮你把生活过得更好。
cues.en: Trying to empower you to make your life better.

cues.zh: 那些让人际连接更难、甚至更随机的技术，呃，
cues.en: Technologies which make human connection harder or even just more random are, uh,

cues.zh: 很糟糕！
cues.en: bad!

cues.zh: 这一点我确实认为是非黑即白的。
cues.en: That I do think is black-and-white true.

cues.zh: 任何介入想互相帮助的人之间的技术，往好了说是令人沮丧，往坏了说是剥削。
cues.en: Any piece of technology which gets in between humans who wish to help each other is frustrating at best and exploitative at worst.

cues.zh: 我们早该明白，这些系统被部署的真正原因，就是为了让助人岗位上需要的人更少。
cues.en: We ought to know by now the real reason those systems get put in place is so that we need fewer humans in helpful roles.

cues.zh: 而且我认为毫无疑问，这只会越来越糟，
cues.en: And I think there is absolutely no question that this is going to get worse

cues.zh: 直到我们所有人开始向内看，开始质疑我们在这个世界上如何行事、以及为什么。
cues.en: until we all start looking inward and begin questioning how we operate in this world and why.

cues.zh: 硅谷似乎铁了心要造出能替我们思考的机器。
cues.en: Silicon valley seems hellbent on creating machines which can do our thinking for us.

cues.zh: 我们为什么会想要那样呢？
cues.en: Why should any of us want that?

cues.zh: 我肯定不想要那样——除非我动脑构建出完整的理解框架，否则我什么都学不到。
cues.en: I certainly don’t want that - I don’t learn anything unless I do the mental work to create a complete framework of understanding in my mind.

cues.zh: 我不谈论自己不懂的东西，因为那是让自己出丑最快的方式。
cues.en: I don’t talk about things I don’t understand because that’s the fastest way you can make a fool of yourself.

cues.zh: 而当你像我这样拥有一个平台时，这可能会很危险。
cues.en: And it can be dangerous when you have a platform like I do.

cues.zh: 我永远不会相信计算机程序能像人一样理解任何事物，
cues.en: I will never trust a computer program to be able to understand anything in the way a human can,

cues.zh: 我也不会信任它替我查找信息。
cues.en: nor will I trust it to find information for me.

cues.zh: 如果我必须核实它找到的每一样东西，那我最终做的还是我自己本来就得做的工作。
cues.en: If I have to vet everything it’s finding, then I end up doing the same work I would have done myself.

cues.zh: 而如果我不核实它找到的东西，那我实际上就是在说，我不想为自己的所作所为负责。
cues.en: And if I don’t vet what it’s finding, then what I’m really doing is saying I don’t want to be responsible for what I do.

cues.zh: 让我感到害怕的是，尽管我们都已看到社交媒体推荐算法在塑造我们观点方面能造成怎样的后果，
cues.en: It frightens me that even though we’ve all seen the consequences of what a social media recommendation algorithm can do to shape our viewpoints

cues.zh: 我们却不知怎地还是落入了机器的诱惑——让机器替我们卸载思考过程。
cues.en: that we are somehow falling for the temptation of machines which can offload our thought processes.

cues.zh: 让我们之所以成为人类的东西。
cues.en: The thing which makes us human.

cues.zh: 如果这都不算最纯粹的懒惰反智主义，我不知道还有什么算。
cues.en: If that’s not the purest form of lazy anti-intellectualism, I don’t know what is.

cues.zh: 在这个愉快的基调上，让我确保你们知道，我和那些真正在努力创造工具解决实际问题的AI研究者一样，对AI炒作周期感到同样的沮丧，
cues.en: On that cheery note, let me make sure you know that I share the same frustration with the AI hype cycle

cues.zh: 比如从图像或血液筛查中早期发现癌症。
cues.en: as the AI researchers who are actually doing work to create tools to solve real problems, like early detection of cancers from images or blood screens.

cues.zh: 那是有价值的研究，无疑将拯救生命。
cues.en: That is valuable research which will undoubtedly save lives.

cues.zh: 令人极其沮丧的是，目前公众意识中唯一存在的AI，是那种能做出一些非常令人印象深刻的花招的AI，
cues.en: It’s beyond frustrating that the only kind of AI that is in the public consciousness at the moment is the one that does some very impressive tricks

cues.zh: 但任何诚实的人都会告诉你，它需要严密监督，因为它会产生幻觉并输出糟糕的结果。
cues.en: but any honest person will tell you needs intense supervision because it will hallucinate and produce bad outputs.

cues.zh: 在我看来这显而易见，
cues.en: It seems blindingly obvious to me

cues.zh: 风险太高了，不能把我们的决策权交给一台无法为其所做决策负责的计算机。
cues.en: that the stakes are way too high to hand over our decision making to a computer which cannot be held responsible for the decisions it makes.

cues.zh: 令人不安的是，我认为这才是想要推动这个未来的真正原因。
cues.en: And that’s, disturbingly, what I think is the real reason for wanting to push this future.

cues.zh: 但你们已经忍受我够久了。
cues.en: But you’ve put up with me long enough.

cues.zh: 感谢观看，希望我听起来不至于太离谱。
cues.en: Thank you for watching and I hope I don’t sound too far off my rocker.

cues.zh: 我开这个频道不只是为了分享我发现的有趣东西，更是为了展示我们过去解决问题的那些惊人方式。
cues.en: I made this channel not just to share cool stuff I find but to show all the amazing ways we solved our problems in the past.

cues.zh: 那里有宝贵的教训，忘了它们后果自负。
cues.en: There are invaluable lessons there which we forget at our peril.

cues.zh: 我不太谈计算机技术，因为它并不怎么让我感兴趣。
cues.en: I don’t talk much about computer technology because it doesn’t really interest me.

cues.zh: 而且随着时间推移，它变得越来越没意思了。
cues.en: And it’s becoming less and less interesting as time goes on.

cues.zh: 除了硬核爱好者或研究海量数据的人之外，
cues.en: Outside of hardcore enthusiasts or people doing research on vast amounts of data,

cues.zh: 说实话：计算已经是个被解决的问题了。
cues.en: let’s be honest: computing is a solved problem.

cues.zh: 我可以用2017年的台式机给你们做这些视频，完全不会碍事，
cues.en: I can use my desktop computer from 2017 to make these videos for you and it would not get in my way at all,

cues.zh: 而我买来随便玩玩的600美元、近乎基础配置的M2 Mac Mini也能做得一样好。
cues.en: and the $600 nearly base-spec M2 Mac Mini I bought to dingle around on can do it just as well.

cues.zh: 视频编码效率越来越高，我们传输这类视频到世界各地所需的带宽和存储越来越少
cues.en: Video encoding is getting more efficient and we need less bandwidth and storage to send videos like this across the world

cues.zh: 尽管互联网连接速度越来越快。
cues.en: and that’s despite internet connections getting faster and faster.

cues.zh: 所以我认为很明显，正是这一现实促使硅谷如今在做这些事情。
cues.en: So I think it’s pretty clear that that reality is why silicon valley is doing the stuff it’s doing these days.

cues.zh: 它必须证明自己是创新中心的合理性，而在这个世界里，它的发展空间正日渐枯竭。
cues.en: It has to justify itself as a center of innovation in a world where it’s running out of runway.

cues.zh: 而它能给出的最佳答案是
cues.en: And the best answer it’s got is

cues.zh: “呃……假装会思考的计算机。”
cues.en: “euhhh computers which pretend to think.”

cues.zh: 恕我直言，我想自己思考。
cues.en: Forgive me, but I want to think for myself.

cues.zh: 我认为你也应该如此。
cues.en: And I think you should, too.
